paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole passage is about: where your trust is sitting. A father brings his suffering son to Jesus, and the disciples couldn't heal the boy. When they ask why, Jesus answers, "Because you have so little faith" (Matthew 17:20). Then He says, "if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you" (Matthew 17:20).

Notice the size Jesus picks. A mustard seed is tiny, so it isn't about having a mountain of faith. It's about putting even a little faith in the right place, and I think that's good news for every baker who feels small. Then Jesus tells His disciples plainly that the Son of Man will be killed and raised on the third day (Matthew 17:22-23). The disciples were deeply grieved, but Jesus said the third day was coming too, and He kept His eyes on that.

The coin in the fish shows the same Jesus. The sons are exempt, and Jesus says so, yet He tells Peter to pay "for My tax and yours" (Matthew 17:25-27). He covers the bill for Peter, and I LOVE that, friend. So trust Him with the mountain, trust Him with the hard news, and trust Him with the bill, because this is the One who has it all in hand.
